(a) SGD converges to a global optimum of the empirical risk minimization objective, (b) the optimum is a network with a generalization error that depends on the data dimensionality and the number of samples, and (c) the network has a small number of nonzeros.

1) SGD can learn overparameterized neural networks on structured data, 2) SGD learns networks with small generalization error even when the networks have enough capacity to fit the labels, 3) the learned networks can be sparse, 4) SGD converges to the learned networks in a few iterations, and 5) the learned networks have small weights.

, in order to learn overparameterized neural networks, SGD does not require the network to be trained with a small learning rate or a large number of iterations.

SGD can learn a network with small generalization error from random initialization, even though the network has enough flexibility to memorize the data, provided that the data comes from well-separated distributions.
